correctness.rationale: I independently rebuilt \(GP(10,2)\), its all-pairs shortest-path metric, and all magnitude chains of length \(4\) in homological degrees \(2,3,4\). The chain dimensions are \(1440,3240,1620\). Direct bit-exact elimination over \(\mathbb F_2\) gives \(\operatorname{rank}\partial_3=1320\) and \(\operatorname{rank}\partial_4=1560\), hence \(3240-1320-1560=360\). The frozen verifier uses the same definitions but independently cross-checks chain counts by dynamic programming and ranks by both column and transposed-row elimination; its certificate agrees. This is exhaustive finite linear algebra, not an extrapolation.
correctness.risk: The result is mod-2 and one bidegree only; it does not determine integral torsion.

originality.rationale: Asao--Hiraoka--Kanazawa prove first-off-diagonal vanishing only when girth is at least seven; the dodecahedral graph has girth five, so their theorem is inapplicable. Gu's full paper computes trees, pawful graphs, the icosahedral graph, and cycles, not the dodecahedral graph. Asao--Wakatsuki determine geodetic spaces, but the dodecahedral graph is not geodetic, as the assigned verifier exhibits two shortest paths between a pair at distance four. Resultary searches found no published exact \((3,4)\) value for this graph.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational magnitude-homology table for small distance-regular graphs may contain the same rank.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is a canonical distance-regular polyhedral graph lying outside the easiest geodetic and high-girth regimes. Its first off-diagonal magnitude-homology rank is a natural exact benchmark for testing the sharpness and scope of general structure theorems, and the complete finite computation is nontrivial.
value.risk: A single mod-2 Betti number has narrower utility than an integral or all-bidegree computation.

final_claim: For the dodecahedral graph \(D=GP(10,2)\) with its shortest-path metric, \(\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{MH}_{3,4}(D;\mathbb F_2)=360\).
limitations: No integral torsion or all-bidegree description is claimed.
